processing: Fully oxidised black tea from a garden sold as certified organic, including a bud-heavy golden tips lot.
harvest_season: Not consistently stated by sellers; as elsewhere in Assam, picking runs from spring into autumn.
appearance_dry: Dark full leaf with gold tips, and in the golden tips lot mostly golden buds.
appearance_liquor: Amber to reddish copper, as is typical of tippy Assam.
appearance_wet: Soft coppery leaf and buds, as with other tippy Assam teas.
taste_profile: A golden tips lot is described with dark chocolate, malt and cocoa on the nose, and molasses, roasted macadamia and a woodsy, resinous sweetness in the cup.

brewing.notes: Western-style. Tippy lots turn sharper when overbrewed, so begin at three minutes and try them without milk first.

vintage_note: Sold by grade or as golden tips, and not always with a harvest date. Like other Assam black teas it is best drunk within a year or two. Check the certificate if the organic label matters to you.
description:
Satrupa is an organic garden in Tinsukia district, in the far east of Assam, known abroad mainly through specialty retailers.

Its best-documented tea is a golden tips lot made mostly of tender buds. The more buds in the mix, the softer and sweeter the cup tends to be, as is usual in Assam.

That lot is described with cocoa, malt, molasses and roasted macadamia, with a woodsy sweetness and a long finish. Tippy lots do not need milk, and long steeps can make them sharp.

Buy by grade and read the description closely, because two teas both labelled Satrupa may be very different drinks.
history: Little is documented about when Satrupa was planted or who has owned it. Its name reaches tea drinkers through importers and retailers in North America and Europe, who sell it as a certified organic single-garden Assam.
